## Load Packages and Source Functions
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(stars)
library(tmap)
library(here)
library(gt)
```

## Import Data

```{r}
# Read in HOLC grade designations for Los Angeles
redline_LA <- sf::st_read(here::here("data", "mapping-inequality", "mapping-inequality-los-angeles.json"))

# Read in ejscreen data 
ej_screen <- sf::st_read(here::here("data", "ejscreen", "EJSCREEN_2023_BG_StatePct_with_AS_CNMI_GU_VI.gdb"))

# Read in crash data
crashes <- read_csv(here::here("data", "SWITRS_LA", "Crashes.csv"))
```

```{r}
# Filter to Los Angeles
los_angeles <- ej_screen |> 
  dplyr::filter(CNTY_NAME == 'Los Angeles County')
```

## Part 1: Legacy of redlining in current environmental (in)justice
```{r}
# Create a map of historical redlining neighborhoods 
grade_colors <- c("#0DB82A", "#0D3DB8","#E0D924","#EB340E")

tm_shape(redline_LA) +
   tm_polygons(
    fill = 'grade',
    fill.scale = tm_scale(values = grade_colors),
    fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "HOLC Grade")) +
    tm_basemap() +
    tm_title("Fig.1 : Historical HOLC Grade Rankings in Los Angeles") +
  tm_scalebar() +
  tm_compass(position = c("left", "top"))

```

```{r}
# Match crs of redline_LA and los_angeles 
st_crs(redline_LA) == st_crs(los_angeles)

redline_LA_transform <- st_transform(redline_LA, crs = st_crs(los_angeles))

# Verify that crs match
if(st_crs(redline_LA) == st_crs(los_angeles)){
  print("CRS MATCH")
}else{
  warning("CRS NOT A MATCH")
}

# Combine datasets
redline_joined <- st_join(redline_LA_transform, los_angeles)
```
```{r}
# Summarise percentage of census block groups in each HOLC grade
percent_HOLC <- redline_joined |> st_drop_geometry() |> 
  group_by(grade) |> 
  summarise(percentage = n()/nrow(redline_joined) * 100)

percent_HOLC |> 
  gt() |> 
    tab_header(title = md("Percentage of Census Block Groups in each HOLC Grade"))
```

```{r}
# Check for NAs
sum(is.na(redline_joined$P_LOWINCPCT))
sum(is.na(redline_joined$P_PM25))
sum(is.na(redline_joined$P_LIFEEXPPCT))

# Calculate mean percentage low income population in each HOLC grade
mean_lowinc <- redline_joined |> 
  group_by(grade) |> 
  summarise(mean_low_inc_PCT = mean(P_LOWINCPCT)) |> 
  st_drop_geometry()

# Visualize the mean percentage low income population per HOLC grade
mean_lowinc |> 
  ggplot(aes(y=mean_low_inc_PCT, x=grade)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity", fill = "#862C4D") +
  labs(title = "Fig.2 : Average Percent Low Income Population Per HOLC Grade", x = "HOLC Grade", y = "Average Percentage Low Income")

# Calculate mean percentile for Particulate Matter 2.5 for each HOLC grade
mean_pm25 <- redline_joined |> 
  group_by(grade) |> 
  summarise(mean_pm_25 = mean(P_PM25)) |> 
  st_drop_geometry()

# Visualize the mean percentile for Particulate Matter 2.5 for each HOLC grade
mean_pm25 |> 
  ggplot(aes(y=mean_pm_25, x=grade)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity", fill = "#507555") +
  labs(title = "Fig.3: Average Percentile for Particulate Matter 2.5 Per HOLC Grade", x = "HOLC Grade", y = "Average Percentile PM2.5")

# Calculate mean percentile for low life expectancy for each HOLC grade
mean_life_exp <- redline_joined |> 
  group_by(grade) |> 
  summarise(mean_life_exp_pct = mean(P_LIFEEXPPCT, na.rm=TRUE)) |> # drop NAs
  st_drop_geometry()

# Visualize the mean percentile for low life expectancy for each HOLC grade
mean_life_exp |> 
  ggplot(aes(y=mean_life_exp_pct, x=grade)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity", fill = "#E18079") +
  labs(title = "Fig.4 : Average Percentile for Low Life Expectancy Per HOLC Grade", x = "HOLC Grade", y = "Average Percentile Low Life Expectancy")
```

### Reflection on Results
Figure 1 shows the distribution of Home Owner’s Loan Corporation (HOLC) grades across the Los Angeles area. In the 1930s , the HOLC graded neighborhoods as either A (green), B (blue), C (yellow) or D (red) corresponding to the perceived risk associated with insuring mortgages, known as “redlining”. Figure 2 represents the mean percentage low income population in each grade in Los Angeles. From this figure, a less favorable HOLC grade is associated with a greater percentage of low income. Figures 3 and 4 display the average percentile per HOLC grade for particulate matter 2.5 and low life expectancy respectively. There is a marked increase in both percentiles as the grade moves from A to D, suggesting a correlation between a less favorable HOLC grade and less favorable environmental and health outcomes. The increase in average percentile for low life expectancy between grades is more sizable than the increase in average percentile for particulate matter 2.5. This may suggest that other factors than particulate matter 2.5 are also impacting the life expectancy. Overall, Figures 1 to 4 demonstrate some of the lasting impacts of the historical practice of “redlining”.

## Part 2: Legacy of redlining in pedestrian and bike accidents

```{r}
# Check for NAs in POINT_X/POINT_Y and LONGITUDE/LATITUDE
sum(crashes$POINT_X == 'NA')
sum(crashes$POINT_Y == 'NA')
sum(crashes$LONGITUDE == 'NA')
sum(crashes$LATITUDE == 'NA')

# Filter crash data to pedestrian or bicycle accidents and filter out NAs
crashes_filtered <- crashes |> 
  filter(PEDESTRIAN_ACCIDENT == "Y" | BICYCLE_ACCIDENT == "Y") |> 
  filter(POINT_X != 'NA')

# Convert X and Y columns to points using WGS 84
crashes_points <- st_as_sf(crashes_filtered, coords = c("POINT_X", "POINT_Y"), crs = 4326)

# Check if crs match
st_crs(redline_joined) == st_crs(crashes_points)

# Match crs and verify match
crashes_transform <- st_transform(crashes_points, crs = st_crs(redline_joined))
if(st_crs(crashes_transform) != st_crs(redline_joined)) stop('Check if CRS match')

# Subset to points in HOLC regions
crashes_holc <- crashes_transform[redline_joined,]

# Join data frames by left join
crashes_lj <- st_join(crashes_holc, redline_joined) |> 
  select(id = ID, region = grade)

# Calculate number of crashes per HOLC grade region
crashes_per_grade <- crashes_lj |>
  filter(!is.na(region)) |> 
  group_by(region) |>
  summarise(number_points = n()) |>
  st_drop_geometry() 

# Calculate percentage crashes in each grade region
crashes_percent_grade <- crashes_per_grade |> 
  mutate(Percentage = 100*(number_points/sum(crashes_per_grade$number_points)))

# Convert region column to factors
crashes_percent_grade$region <- as.factor(crashes_percent_grade$region)

# Visualize the percentage crashes per HOLC region
crashes_percent_grade |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = region, y = Percentage, fill = region))+
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "#9EC0EB") +
  labs(title = "Percentage Bike and Pedestrian Crashes and Fatalities Within Each HOLC Grade", x = "Grade" , y = "Percentage Pedestrian and Bicycle Accidents")
```
